wstep: This card describes NCHFP tomato juice, hot packed and processed in a boiling-water bath with added acid. [T:ACI-051]

akapity: According to an FDA list, tomatoes have an approximate pH of 4.30–4.90, and the value varies widely with variety and conditions. [T:ACI-093]
Sugar may be added to balance the acidic taste, but the acid must not be left out. [T:ACI-047]
Add 2 tablespoons of bottled lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid per quart jar (about 0.95 l) of juice. [T:ACI-044]
For pint jars, use 1 tablespoon of bottled lemon juice or 1/4 teaspoon of citric acid. [T:ACI-045]
Do not can tomatoes from dead or frost-killed vines. [T:ACI-049]
Add the bottled lemon juice or citric acid to the jars, heat the juice to boiling again and fill the jars with hot juice, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-171]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) above sea level, process the juice in a boiling-water bath for 35 minutes in pint jars and 40 minutes in quart jars. [T:ACI-051,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints for 40 minutes and quarts for 45. [T:ACI-172,ACI-176]
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints for 45 minutes and quarts for 50. [T:ACI-177,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints for 50 minutes and quarts for 55. [T:ACI-178,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml. [T:ACI-174]
For a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time. [T:ACI-175]
NCHFP gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so use smaller jars. [T:ACI-175]
